notes: Introduced versioned self-update: added VERSION and CHANGELOG.json, and the -update command.
Fixed -update writing files with a UTF-8 BOM (Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 adds one on Windows PowerShell), which corrupted synced files with a stray character and noisy diffs.

Split project types into config/projectTypes.json (built-in, synced by -update) and config/projectTypes.local.json (your saved types, never touched by -update). Previously -update would have overwritten any custom project type you saved.

Fixed -update's release-notes step throwing on Windows PowerShell 5.1: wrapping ConvertFrom-Json's array output in @() could collapse a multi-entry CHANGELOG.json into a single flattened item. Now fetches the raw text and parses it directly.
The -new wizard's project folder step now shows a selection menu of the subfolders under devDirectory, with an 'Enter custom path...' option to fall back to free text.

MyShortcuts.ps1's -d now always opens the MyShortcuts folder in the terminal and lists it (the -terminal/-t switch was removed). Added a new -e/-explorer switch to open the folder in Windows Explorer instead. The -edit command's -e alias was removed to free up -e for this.
Updated README.md and CLAUDE.md to document the -d/-e change from 1.0.5 (README's usage table and CLAUDE.md's manager description previously still referenced the removed -t switch).

Split features into config/features.json (built-in, synced by -update) and config/features.local.json (your own custom features, never touched by -update), merged at runtime by Get-MergedFeatures. This mirrors the projectTypes.json/.local split and lets a downstream fork carry custom features that survive updates from upstream. If you have no features.local.json, behavior is unchanged.
Renamed the 'open solution' switch from -project/-p to -solution/-sln.

The solution feature now finds the solution automatically: at run time it opens an explicitly configured $sln if present, otherwise auto-detects a solution file in the project folder, preferring the modern .slnx over .sln. Compile (-release/-debug) uses the same detection. The -new wizard proposes an existing solution file it finds in the chosen folder (Enter = use existing <file>).
Added a data-driven 'detect' field for feature prompts (array of glob patterns) that powers the wizard's solution proposal; documented in CLAUDE.md.
Project types: dropped tunnel and azurite from the pre-checked .NET set, and merged the identical Node.js and Python types into a single 'Simple - editor-centric' type.

Added a 'push' feature (-push / -gp): runs git add -A, prompts for a commit message (aborts if empty), commits and pushes, in the project directory. Not part of -all by default. Pre-checked in the .NET and Simple project types.

Fixed -edit (Add predefined feature) not honoring a prompt's 'detect' field: adding the solution/compile feature to an existing script now proposes an existing .slnx/.sln found in the project folder (Enter = use existing <file>), matching the -new wizard. Previously it fell through to a plain prompt.

Reworked 'push': removed it as a per-project feature and added it as a MyShortcuts manager command instead. Run 'MyShortcuts -push' (alias -p) to back up the MyShortcuts folder itself to GitHub — git add -A, prompts for a commit message (aborts if empty), commits and pushes. Use it after -new/-edit to save your shortcut scripts to your fork. If you added the old per-project push feature to a shortcut, that script keeps working; the feature is just no longer offered by -new/-edit.

The -new wizard's folder step is now a navigator: '..' walks up (past the base folder too), subfolders descend on Enter, '[ Select this folder ]' picks the current folder, and '[ Enter path manually... ]' still lets you type a path. The chosen folder is always saved as an ABSOLUTE path in $projectDir, so a shortcut keeps working even if devDirectory later moves.
Project-type menu reordered: your own saved (local) types now appear on top, newest first, and 'Blank — start from scratch' is always last.

Explorer shortcut is now -x everywhere: 'MyShortcuts -x' opens the MyShortcuts folder, and the per-project explorer feature uses -x (previously -e for the manager and -exp for scripts). Existing generated scripts keep their old -exp switch until re-created.
The wizard only offers to save your selection as a project type when you actually changed it from the chosen type's defaults, instead of asking every time.
The custom-command prompt now shows (y/N) with No as the default (pressing Enter skips).

Reverted the -new folder navigator added in 1.0.12: the folder step is back to the original single-select list of your devDirectory's immediate subfolders plus 'Enter custom path...'. A relative name resolves under devDirectory and an absolute path is stored as-is, exactly as before 1.0.12.
Added an -e alias for the -edit command (freed up now that explorer uses -x).
Added a -help / -h command that prints a summary of all commands and their aliases. Running MyShortcuts with no switch now shows this help instead of a one-line hint.

The claude feature now runs Claude Code in the current terminal and drops the pushd/popd wrapper, so the terminal stays in the project directory after you exit Claude. Re-create or re-add the feature to a shortcut to pick up the change.

Fixed PATH registration duplicating the entire Machine PATH into the User PATH: Check-EnvPath now reads the User-scope registry value directly instead of the merged session $Env:Path (which combines Machine + User). Does not retroactively clean an already-polluted User PATH.

PATH registration is no longer automatic on every run. Added -init / -i: run it to add the MyShortcuts folder to your PATH if it isn't already there. Every other command now just prints a one-line warning when PATH isn't set up, instead of silently rewriting it.
